newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Product Swaps - Gas oil edges up on crude.
newsitem.headline: Asia Product Swaps - Gas oil edges up on crude.

text.p: Singapore gas oil swaps edged up slightly in quiet trading on firmer crude prices late afternoon on Friday in the absence of fresh physical market indicators, traders said.
"Gas oil is firming because of crude. There are changes to the fundamentals and people are still expecting the local traders to continue buying," one trader said.
The front month April gas oil swaps was last quoted unchanged from Thursday at $26.50/$26.70 per barrel, brokers said.

On Thursday, one trader bought 150,000-barrels at $27.10 per barrel for April 25-29 lifting free-on-board (fob) Singapore, and another at $26.70 for May 6-10 lifting fob, both from a European major, mirroring traded levels seen this week.

The fuel oil swaps were firmer following the stronger crude with April last quoted at $98.50/$99.25 per tonne. May swaps traded at $97.50 per tonne earlier in the day, up about 50 cents from Thursday's traded level, brokers said.
But May swaps were up about 20 cents at $25.50/$25.70, they said.
Overnight May Brent crude closed up 16 cents to $17.93 per barrel on London's International Petroleum Exchange and extended its rally on Friday to last trade up 12 cents.
Traders said the market is not likely to break from the current high trading range as the buying spree of two local traders is expected to persist for the rest of this month.
The two related local traders have have already bought more 11 million barrels of physical gas oil since March 3. -- Singapore Newsroom (+65-870 3093)
